conflicts: Brief Alignment proposes: Retain the dominant sphere, rich chromatic cells, dark stage, and full control panel, but make the cellular automaton legible: organize cells on a visible curved lattice or latitude/longitude topology, show clustered live/dead neighborhoods and a few emergent structures rather than uniform random scatter, and label the topology as seamless spherical wrapping. Additional literal detail can increase one-off components and rough exceptions unless each addition is expressed through the established construction system. Clarity proposes: Bind the visualization information into one region by aligning the title directly above the sphere and grouping active cells, surface density, and topology in a compact caption immediately below it. Changing scale and contrast for hierarchy is useful, but ad hoc emphasis must not introduce unrelated borders, shadows, typography, or spacing. Expressiveness proposes: Carry cellular motifs into the controls through tiny state patterns, evolving swatches, and a generation pulse; vary clusters by age or lineage rather than random color alone; and add a restrained halo or orbit annotation that makes the spherical Life concept uniquely identifiable. Extra shapes, textures, glows, and differentiated treatments can fragment palette, geometry, and material logic if each becomes a bespoke exception.
accept: Accept every fidelity restoration, hierarchy correction, and thematic differentiation that can be built from shared grid, type, palette, stroke, radius, elevation, and illustration tokens. compromise: Implement the craft foundation first: Mask and warp the grid and cells cleanly to the sphere, add a controlled atmospheric rim, and explicitly split orbital lines into behind/in-front segments so every intersection is intentional.
